name: TT-Metal's decode attention kernel only implements multi-query attention
symptom: A decode attention call that is fast on a multi-query model does not accept a grouped-query model on the same kernel. The scaled-dot-product attention decode op states that its implementation is Flash-Decode and that it currently only supports MQA while decoding a single token. Query heads are not a parallelization axis; the op parallelizes over the batch and over the K/V sequence length, and the output head count is the query head count padded up to the tile height rather than a real multi-head result.
root_cause: Decode attention on one token is bandwidth-bound, so the kernel spends its cores on reading more of the KV cache in parallel and reducing the partial softmax statistics over the on-chip network, instead of on computing many query heads. That split only pays when every core in a group reads the same K and V, which is exactly multi-query attention. Grouped-query attention breaks the assumption: cores working on different query heads within a group still share K and V, but the kernel has no path to multicast one K and V head to several query heads. The 2024 Wormhole FlashAttention report names that multicast as future work and does not implement it.
workaround: Lower grouped-query attention to multi-query attention for the decode step by repeating the KV head across the group, and accept the extra KV bandwidth that costs, or keep grouped-query attention and write the multicast the report describes: one core reads the K and V head and the on-chip network delivers it to the cores holding the query heads of that group. For the chunk size, leave the default alone unless measuring — unpaged decode uses min(512, the largest power-of-two divisor of the sequence length), and paged decode uses 32 when no program config is passed.
notes: The constraint is the vendor's own statement on the SDPA decode API page, read 2026-10-17, not an inference from the kernel source. It is the decode-side counterpart of [[tt-metal-flash-decode-kv-split]]: the same kernel family that is 20x faster than unfused attention in prefill ([[papers/tt-metal-flashattention-wormhole]]) will not run a grouped-query decode at all. Most models shipped since Llama-2 use grouped-query attention, so this is the common case rather than an edge case.
